content:
Your church's books need to show what came in, what went out, and where each transaction belongs. A bookkeeper records and checks that work; accounting software holds the records and produces reports.

Choose them together under your Financial Leader's oversight. Start with the church's financial policies, then ask candidates to show how they would record transactions, explain differences, and prepare reports for the people authorized to see them.

---

## Start with the federal recordkeeping rule

The IRS requires tax-exempt organizations, including churches, to maintain accounting books and other records supporting their exemption and any required federal returns. Records of activities, income, and expenses are still necessary when no return is filed.

The IRS does not prescribe a specific recordkeeping format. Its examples include ledgers, receipts and disbursements journals, payroll and banking records, and invoices. Choose a system that can keep those records available for examination rather than assuming a product's church label establishes compliance.

---

## Define the work before seeking help

Write down which tasks you want the bookkeeper to perform. The Bureau of Labor Statistics describes transaction entry, account coding, accuracy checks, reconciliation, and financial reporting as typical bookkeeping work. Payroll may be an additional responsibility; ask whether it is included.

Use the church's existing separation of duties when assigning that work. Keep responsibility for counting, recording, disbursing, and approving in the roles established by your financial policies. The Financial Leader oversees accounting under the elders' direction.

If you outsource payroll, retain church oversight of tax deposits. The IRS says the employer remains responsible for federal tax liabilities when a payroll service fails to pay them. Ask how your church will verify deposits independently.

---

## Ask candidates to show their work

Use the duties you listed as interview prompts. Ask a candidate to explain how they assign a receipt or bill to an account, check the entry, and investigate a difference between records. Ask them to walk you through a financial report they would prepare for your Financial Leader.

Look for evidence of accounting-software skills, attention to detail, and confidentiality. BLS identifies these as important qualities for bookkeepers. Ask how the candidate would protect individual giving records while making authorized financial reporting available.

For church-specific work, ask about experience with your fund structure and any payroll responsibilities you propose to assign. Keep clergy payroll questions with the separately reviewed payroll process.

<Callout type="scripture">
*"In this case, moreover, it is required of stewards that one be found faithful."* — 1 Corinthians 4:2 (LSB)
</Callout>

---

## Compare fund tracking and reports

Bring your approved fund list and budget to a demonstration. Your designated-giving policy calls for separate tracking of each fund's income, expenses, and balance. Ask to see those results in the proposed system.

| Ask to see | What to examine |
|---|---|
| Fund activity | Beginning balance, income, expenses, transfers, and ending balance |
| Budget comparison | Actual results beside the budget for the same period |
| Leadership reports | Financial information without individual donor details |
| Downloaded reports | Files your authorized reviewer can open and read |

Ask the demonstrator to explain any difference between funds and project tags or categories. In the documentation reviewed for this guide, tags track income and expenses but do not appear on the balance sheet like funds. Check the proposed product's behavior directly.

---

## Check access against church policy

Have the Financial Leader review permissions before inviting users. Follow the existing accountability policy, including its limits on the Senior Pastor's financial access and its confidentiality rules for individual giving.

Ask the vendor to demonstrate the roles available in the exact subscription under consideration. Check who can enter accounting records, approve bills, read reports, and manage users. Test the proposed reviewer's access rather than giving everyone administrator permissions.

<Callout type="warning">
Do not replace the church's payment approvals with permission to use accounting software. Follow the existing disbursement policy when deciding who initiates and who approves a payment.
</Callout>

For a product with electronic bill approval, ask to see the approval status and the steps between receiving a bill and paying it.

---

## Try a sample workflow

Use this exercise to evaluate the candidate and software together:

- [ ] Enter a sample gift into an approved fund and locate its accounting entry.
- [ ] Enter a sample bill against the appropriate expense account and fund.
- [ ] Show how the bill follows your church's approval process.
- [ ] Import a sample bank transaction and check the target register and coding.
- [ ] Compare the deposit with the giving record and investigate any difference.
- [ ] Produce the fund and budget reports your reviewer needs.
- [ ] Export a report and open the downloaded file.

Ask what happens when your bank connection is unavailable or older transactions are needed. The bank-integration documentation reviewed here offers file import as an alternative; confirm the options for your own bank and proposed software.

<Callout type="tip">
Ask the candidate to explain an unexplained difference rather than simply changing an entry to make totals match. Checking accuracy and reporting differences are part of the bookkeeping work described by BLS.
</Callout>

---

## Compare the complete scope and cost

Ask for a proposal matching the tasks and features you demonstrated. Identify what the bookkeeper will handle and which work remains with the church or another provider.

Check the subscription's included users, permission controls, budgeting, and bill-approval options. Product documentation may place these in different plans or add-ons. Ask separately about setup work, including the chart of accounts, funds, starting balances, and training.

<Callout type="important">
Federal guidance and product documentation checked October 16, 2026. Confirm current recordkeeping guidance with the IRS. Confirm features, subscription terms, and any additional charges with each vendor before purchasing.
</Callout>

---

## Plan the handoff

Document the bookkeeping procedures so another authorized person can follow them. Include the records used, account and fund assignments, review steps, and reports to prepare. Keep supporting records with the accounting work.

Before a bookkeeper leaves, have the Financial Leader check the records and unresolved differences with them. Confirm that the church's authorized people can retrieve reports and manage account access. Ask the vendor to show how to disable or remove a departing user's access.

Keep a church-controlled copy of exported reports and the underlying supporting records. The IRS's recordkeeping obligation remains with the organization, and a report download alone does not replace its receipts, invoices, banking records, or other necessary documentation.
excerpt: Choose bookkeeping help and accounting software by checking responsibilities, fund reports, access, costs, and a sample workflow.
title: Choosing a Bookkeeper and Accounting Software

sources.claim: Opening and sections 2, 3, 6: bookkeepers enter and code transactions, check accuracy, reconcile or report differences, and prepare reports; payroll is a possible additional task. Interview questions and sample exercise apply these duties, not a statutory hiring standard. BLS also identifies computer skills, attention to detail and confidentiality.
sources.quote:
Enter (post) financial transactions into the appropriate computer software
Put costs (debits) and income (credits) into the software, assigning each to an appropriate account
Check for accuracy in figures, postings, and reports
Reconcile or note and report any differences they find in the records
These workers also may take on additional tasks, such as payroll, billing, purchasing, and keeping track of overdue bills.
Computer skills. Bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks need to be comfortable using computer spreadsheets and bookkeeping software.
Integrity. Bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks have control of an organization’s financial documentation, which they must use properly and keep confidential.
Detail oriented. Bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks are responsible for producing accurate financial records, which requires them to pay close attention in order to recognize and avoid making errors.

sources.claim: Section 1 and final paragraph: churches must retain books supporting exemption and required returns; the IRS prescribes no specific format and lists underlying records. Software labels and exported reports are not substitutes for those records. Only recordkeeping passage on printed p.25 used; older filing deadlines in this publication are not used.
sources.publisher: Internal Revenue Service, Publication 1828, printed page 25
sources.quote:
All tax-exempt organizations, including churches and religious organizations (regardless of whether tax-exempt status has been officially recognized by the IRS), are required to maintain books of accounting and other records necessary to justify their claim for exemption in the event of an audit.
There is no specific format for keeping records. However, the types of required records frequently include organizing documents (charter, constitution, articles of incorporation) and bylaws, minute books, property records, general ledgers, receipts and disbursements journals, payroll records, banking records and invoices.

sources.claim: Section 1 and handoff: even with no return, maintain activity, income and expense records; records must be available for IRS inspection. The refresh callout directs current guidance checks to the agency.
sources.quote:
Remember, even if 990-N is filed, or no return is filed, records must be maintained showing activities conducted, income received and expenses incurred.
Books and records must be available for inspection by the IRS.

sources.claim: Section 2: outsourcing payroll does not remove employer federal tax responsibility; independent deposit verification.
sources.quote:
The employer is ultimately responsible for the deposit and payment of federal tax liabilities.
Employers should register on the EFTPS system to get their own PIN and use this PIN to periodically verify payments.

sources.claim: Opening, sections 2, 3, 4, 5 and 8: existing EveryField policy assigns accounting oversight to the Financial Leader under elders; separates roles, protects donor confidentiality and limits Senior Pastor access; documents procedures and review. Read from the local seed at the pinned commit before drafting. The policy is an existing methodology, not a new legal mandate.
sources.publisher: EveryField, published Principles of Financial Accountability
sources.quote:
Establish a Financial Leader immediately—someone who takes ownership of financial operations under the direction of the elders.
Document procedures so they're not dependent on one person
Those who count should not also enter data into the accounting system.
Those who record income should not also write checks.
Those who request purchases should not approve their own requests.
should be confidential, known only to those with legitimate need (typically the Financial Leader and giving administrator).
| The Senior Pastor Should... | The Senior Pastor Should NOT... |
| Review financial reports | Have bank account access |

sources.claim: Section 4 approved fund list and separate tracking: existing designated giving policy. Sections 2, 5 and 6 retain disbursement approvals. Read local seed at pinned commit.
sources.publisher: EveryField, published Designated Giving Policies and Disbursements and Approvals
sources.quote:
Each designated fund should be tracked separately in your accounting system:
- Separate account or fund code
- Income tracked by fund
- Expenses tracked by fund
- Balance readily available
One person initiates payment in system
Second person reviews and approves

sources.claim: Sections 2 and 3: clergy payroll stays with existing specialized workflow rather than implying routine bookkeeping covers clergy tax decisions. Read local seed at pinned commit.
sources.publisher: EveryField, published Setting Up Payroll for Church Staff
sources.quote: Ask your CPA or payroll provider to review the minister's credentials and duties against Publication 517.

sources.claim: Scripture callout: exact single verse checked by opening the LSB URL directly with HTTP after the web tool could not load it. No theological interpretation added.
sources.publisher: The Lockman Foundation / Three Sixteen Publishing, Legacy Standard Bible
sources.quote: In this case, moreover, it is required of stewards that one be found faithful.

sources.claim: Sections 4 and 6: fund activity report fields; gift records can differ from accounting because donations are unposted. Asking to locate entries tests that relationship. Feature evidence only, no vendor accounting/legal advice adopted.
sources.quote:
starting balance, total income, total expenses, transfers, and the ending balance.
Unposted Donations: Aplos lets you manage donations separately from accounting.

sources.claim: Section 4: ask how tags differ from funds in proposed software, narrowly describing reviewed product documentation rather than all software.
sources.quote: Tags are an optional tracking tool for income and expenses—they do not appear on the Balance Sheet like Funds do.

sources.claim: Sections 4 and 6: budget comparison demonstrations examine actuals against the same period budget.
sources.quote:
The report gives equal prominence to "Current Period" and "Year-to-Date" (YTD) figures.
Current Period: Uses your specific monthly budget.

sources.claim: Sections 4, 6 and 8: accounting software can generate and export reports for authorized readers; ask to open exported reports. No claim that an export includes a complete database or attachments.
sources.quote:
All of the reports can be exported or printed
Each report has the option to Print, Export, or Share by Email

sources.claim: Sections 5 and 8: role and read-only controls are demonstrated against church policy; ask how to disable or remove access.
Section 7: setup proposal questions reflect documented implementation tasks without assuming they are included in ordinary bookkeeping.
sources.quote: importing your Chart of Accounts, creating your Funds, setting up starting balances, and providing tailored training.

sources.claim: Sections 5, 6 and 7: electronic bill workflow and approval status are features to verify in proposed plan; ask about subscription charges rather than quote amounts.
sources.quote:
The system sends the bills to the approvers for electronic approval and tracks the status of approvals.
Bill Approval is an add-on feature

sources.claim: Section 6: bank transaction coding, target register checks and file import alternative; exercise is a proposed demonstration, not a promise for every product.
sources.quote:
For each transaction, assign the correct Account and Fund (and Payee, if needed).
you can import a file of transactions instead.

sources.claim: Section 7: compare included users, permissions, budgeting and approval across plans; verify current vendor terms. No numerical pricing, promotion or winner is stated.
sources.quote:
Includes 2 Users
Basic Budgeting
User Roles & Permissions
Bill Approval
Additional users

claim_check.notes: Author researched and mapped claims; independent Opus source, scripture and screenshot review required. Accessed 2026-10-16 UTC. ECFA pages returned errors, so no claims rely on their snippets. The only lint warning is "moreover" inside the exact LSB scripture quotation; retained verbatim.

rulings: Resolved: phase 0 follows the existing financial section.
Resolved: preserve existing Financial Leader, Senior Pastor, donor confidentiality and approval policies; no new methodology or legal controls invented.

Resolved: vendor-neutral body with feature demonstrations, no vendor rankings or prices. Vendor documents establish available feature types only, not guarantees for every product. Interview questions and the sample workflow are applications of cited duties and documented features.
Resolved: ECFA search results were not usable evidence because pages could not be opened; omitted them. No state example or jurisdiction-specific requirement is needed.
Resolved: no fee, retention-period, deadline or hiring credential threshold is introduced. Clergy tax settings and donation substantiation remain with existing articles.
Resolved: all external sources and one LSB verse opened personally; local published seed read at pinned source commit before writing. Current guidance and feature descriptions checked 2026-10-16 UTC.
